newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar claws back as Cenbnk intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar claws back as Cenbnk intervenes.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar clawed back morning losses with Central Bank help to close at 469.25/470.50 per dollar after investors sold bolivars on rumors of a cabinet shake-up, traders said.
The unit closed on Wednesday at 467.50/468.75 per dollar.
"It was a speculation driven market that topped at 473/474 bolivars per dollar on news that (Planning Minister) Teodoro Petkoff may be resigning," said one trader.
Petkoff later roundly denied rumors, first published in a local tabloid newspaper, that he might resign.
Traders said the bolivar's weakness was further aggravated by lack of fresh dollar supplies, which dried-up on Wednesday ahead of a four percentage point drop in TEM yields.
"Dollars were in short supply everywhere," said one trader.
